landing-display.purpose: The landing hero headline only: two lines, the second in Instrument Blue.

landing-headline.purpose: Landing section titles and the closing call to action.

landing-title.purpose: Sub-heads within a landing section (Today, Not yet).

landing-lede.purpose: The hero subhead, 34em max; section intros run at 1.125rem, 62ch max.

landing-body.purpose: Landing paragraphs, 36em max in two-column sections.

landing-small.purpose: Nav links, form notes, captions, checks-panel rows, step descriptions.

landing-label.purpose: Form labels; a parenthesised hint follows at 400 in Muted Slate.

landing-micro.purpose: Table heads, scale labels, the checks panel case line, step numbers.

landing-figure.purpose: Measured values: tabular, with unit and limit.

editor-title.purpose: The step title, the one heading in the side panel (--fs-title).

editor-body.purpose: The editor default, buttons included (--fs-body); tabular figures throughout.

editor-label.purpose: Section labels inside a step and the legend title, sentence case, Muted Slate (--fs-small).

editor-small.purpose: Field labels, hints, read-outs, legend text, warnings.

editor-micro.purpose: Badges, step notes, the tooth chart jaw labels and key (--fs-micro).

shadows.name: landing-frame
shadows.purpose: Framed product shots and the gate table; the 1px ring is the hairline edge (--shadow). The session screens borrow it for the hero render beside the sign-in form.

shadows.name: landing-overlay
shadows.purpose: The checks panel where it overlaps the hero render.

shadows.name: landing-inset-card
shadows.purpose: The draft-review crop that sits inside the hero render.

shadows.name: editor-none
shadows.purpose: The editor is flat: tone and 1px hairlines carry depth. The tooth chart inset ring (inset 0 0 0 2px) marks the active tooth and is not elevation.

motion.name: landing-ease-out
motion.purpose: Landing state transitions: buttons 160ms (background, border, transform), pass ticks 240ms fill and 320ms stroke draw after 80ms.

motion.name: landing-count-in
motion.value: 320ms exponential ease-out per value; rows 360ms apart from 450ms
motion.purpose: The checks panel runs once on load, from each gate threshold to its measured value, then holds still. Skipped under reduced motion.

motion.name: landing-field
motion.purpose: Input border colour on hover and focus.

motion.name: editor-standard
motion.purpose: Editor background, border and colour changes on buttons, dropzone and chart keys.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Landing under prefers-reduced-motion: final values, no count-in, no smooth scroll.

narrative.overview:
DentalCAD is a precision instrument that shows its working. It has two surfaces. The landing page (`apps/web/index.html`) persuades a lab technician or clinician on a first visit. The editor at `/app/` is where they then work all day. Both play the category standard straight, at the craft level of exocad, Dentbird and Linear / Vercel: cool white and blue-grey grounds, a single blue, hairlines instead of boxes, and numbers set as numbers. Every claim on screen is something the user can check: a measured value with its unit, a pass mark, a colour map with its scale.

The two surfaces share one look and differ in density. Both are light, set in Hanken Grotesk with deep navy ink and Muted Slate. The landing world has a white ground and display sizes tracked tight. Its sections breathe, and it shows real captures of the editor in a hairline frame with one soft, navy-tinted shadow. The screens between the two (sign-in, create account, the case list) belong to the landing world: its bar and wordmark, its display heading, 44px fields and 8px corners, and the hero render beside the sign-in form. The editor world is dense and flat: instrument sizes (13px body), tonal panels and hairline borders, built for long sessions zoomed into one tooth. Its dark theme is an opt-in from the toolbar (2026-10-26: one look across the surfaces, `specs/2026-10-26-one-look.md`). Both use the same blue (#2f6fde) as their only accent. Both use the same Viewport Grey behind the 3D scene, and the same colour-map stops, which the engine owns and every surface copies.

Ownership: the landing sections of this file are recorded from `apps/web/src/landing/landing.css`, and its direction contract is `apps/web/.impeccable/surfaces/index-html.md`. The parts marked "editor" are **maintained by the editor polish work** (`specs/2026-10-25-ux-critique-polish.md`), recorded from `apps/web/src/styles.css` and `apps/web/src/ui/**/*.css`. Editor token changes land there first and are recorded here afterwards. The colour-map stops belong to `apps/web/src/engine/colormap.ts` and `apps/web/src/tools/crownLegend.ts`. The confirmed visual rejection (PRODUCT.md, Brand Commitments) is that marketing surfaces carry real product renders, never illustration, a glowing-tooth hero or stock clinic photography.
keyCharacteristics: One blue accent (#2f6fde) on both surfaces. Everything else is a neutral, a status or data.
Measurements in tabular figures, always with their unit, and their limit where one exists.
Hairlines and tone for structure. Shadows appear only on the landing page's framed renders and the overlays that sit on them.
Colour maps are clinical data, transcribed exactly from the engine, never decoration.
Real product renders, never illustration, on marketing surfaces.
Dashed and dotted strokes mean not there yet, or a target.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Instrument Blue is the only hue on any surface that is not a status or data colour. There is no second brand colour, no per-section accent and no coloured icon set.

rules.name: The Tint Is Not The Fill Rule
rules.body: The solid accent marks the main action: one per step, form or page region. Repeating the same action is fine: the nav and the hero form both create a lab account. Pressed toggles, the active step, the current unit and drafts take the Blue Wash with Deep Instrument Blue text. Outside actions, the solid accent fills only the tooth chart's marks for what is in the case: crown teeth and their connectors.

rules.name: The Data Is Not Decoration Rule
rules.body: A map colour always means a clinical value. Map colours appear on the scan or crown surface, on the legend and on scales transcribed from it, and nowhere else; the axis colours appear only on the viewport's frame arrows, their swatches and the crown's move handles (mesial-distal green, buccal orange, occlusal blue; a hovered handle turns Draft Amber #ffd166). Penetration Red (#c0392b) is the crown maps' one warning colour.

rules.name: The Tabular Measurement Rule
rules.body: Every millimetre, count, threshold and step number is set in tabular figures with its unit. The editor sets `tabular-nums` on the body. The landing page sets it on every measured value, and puts the limit beside the value in the muted ink (1.01 mm, min 0.50).

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Headings, labels, buttons and section labels are in sentence case at normal or negative tracking. Hierarchy comes from weight and the muted ink, never from uppercase or letter-spacing.

rules.name: The Navy Shadow Rule
rules.body: Landing shadows are tinted with Deep Navy Ink (rgb 15 27 45), never black. They fall straight down with a negative spread and are never offset sideways.

rules.name: The Flat Instrument Rule
rules.body: The editor has no drop shadows. Panels sit on the bench by tone and hairline. The legend floats over the viewport on a 94% Panel White with a hairline. The tooth chart's 2px inset ring marks the active tooth; it is not elevation.

rules.name: The Dashed Means Not-There Rule
rules.body: Dashed and dotted strokes mark what is not there yet, or not there at all: the dropzone and the drop-to-import overlay, a draft step's dot, a check not yet measured, the first-run empty case list, a pontic (a missing tooth being replaced), an unavailable connector, and the dotted target tick on a map scale. Solid strokes mean measured or committed, such as the solid tick at contact or at the minimum.

dos: **Do** use Instrument Blue (#2f6fde) as the only accent, with Deep Instrument Blue (#1f56b8) where blue is text on a tint.
**Do** set every measurement in tabular figures with its unit, and its limit beside it where one exists (1.01 mm, min 0.50).
**Do** show the product through real captures of the editor on the synthetic case, framed on Viewport Grey (#e9ecf0) with the Frame shadow, each with its provenance sidecar.
**Do** copy the colour-map stops, their re-centred positions and the solid and dotted ticks from `colormap.ts` and `crownLegend.ts` whenever a map or scale appears.
**Do** give each step, form or page region one solid-accent action; pressed, active and draft states take the Blue Wash.
**Do** separate with hairlines (#e4e8ee on the landing page, #dde1e6 in the editor) before reaching for a box or a shadow.
**Do** draw icons as authored SVG in `currentColor`, with the control naming the action.

**Do** build new editor screens from the editor's tokens (`--fs-*`, `--radius-sm`, `--radius`, `--control-h`, `--field-border`, `--field-bg`, `--accent-strong`, `--accent-tint`, `--focus-ring`, `--ok`, `--warn-*`), and give every new colour its dark value alongside the light one.
**Do** honour reduced motion with the final state: no count-in, no smooth scroll, and 0ms transitions on the landing page.
donts: **Don't** add a second accent hue, or use a map colour (Penetration Red, Straw, Teal, map Amber) as a UI or brand colour.
**Don't** put illustration, stock clinic photography or a glowing-tooth hero on a marketing surface.
**Don't** set labels in uppercase with wide tracking, or add eyebrow or kicker labels above headings; hierarchy comes from weight and the muted ink.
**Don't** use Unicode glyphs (✓ ✗ ⚠ ↶) as icons or status marks.
**Don't** mark a callout, card or row with a coloured side stripe; a callout is a tinted ground, with at most a hairline all round.
**Don't** use gradient text, or blended gradients on buttons, panels or section grounds; the only blended gradient is a colour-map scale.
**Don't** give editor surfaces drop shadows, and don't use black or sideways-offset shadows on the landing page.
**Don't** use dashed or dotted strokes as decoration; they mean not there yet, or a target.
